title: Kathleen Booth and the First Assembly Language (Late 1940s)
explainer: Mathematician Kathleen Booth, working on early computers at Birkbeck College London in the late 1940s, is widely credited with devising the first assembly language - a mnemonic 'contracted notation' for instructions - along with the first assembler program to translate it into raw numeric machine code. Her work shows assembly language wasn't a later convenience bolted onto computing; it appeared almost as soon as programmable machines did, because writing and debugging programs directly in binary was immediately recognized as impractical.
